# 6. Interaction Flow

## 6.1. Overall Complaint Handling Process

In the home broadband complaint handling system, the complaint handling agent automatically analyzes user complaints and correlates them with known or common issues (e.g., weak WiFi signals), non-network-related issues (e.g., user equipment configuration errors), and network-related issues (e.g., fiber interruptions) to enable automated processing. After classifying network issues, the complaint handling agent collaborates with single-domain fault agents or network optimization agents to perform root cause localization of the complaint. Subsequently, the system provides resolution suggestions, such as adjusting router channels or restarting the optical modem, to achieve automated closed-loop resolution and provide closed-loop verification functionality. The system adopts an agent-based diagnostic model and integrates the Copilot H5 plugin/LPI mode to enhance processing efficiency and accuracy.

Taking ZTE as an example, its complaint handling process begins with complaint analysis to determine whether there is a service interruption or quality issue. This is followed by fault localization. Once localization is complete, the issue is sent to the professional workbench interface for further root cause identification. Based on the fault localization results, the system determines whether the issue can be resolved through automated optimization or remote handling. For issues that cannot be resolved automatically or remotely, the system generates a maintenance work order and sends it to the relevant maintenance department for on-site handling.
